There is deliberately no LOCAL_CI_ENABLED kill switch: a disabled CI would
hand the merge gate a green light it never earned.  See local/protocols/ci.md.

review.sh — model-backed review of a GitHub PR, chained after a green CI.
Account routing passes MIPSTARRE_CODEX_ACCOUNT, MIPSTARRE_ACCOUNT_WAIT and
MIPSTARRE_CODEX_HOME_SECOND through unchanged to dispatch.sh.

Usage:
  local/bin/review.sh <pr-number> [--force-review] [--dry-run]

  <pr-number>      GitHub PR number ("12").  Branch, base and head SHA come
                   from gh_common.py pr-view; the local branch tip must be
                   exactly the GitHub head before anything is reviewed.
  --force-review   Review even when the head commit is a bot fix commit.
                   Used by autofix.sh for the single forced review at the
                   iteration cap (local/protocols/autofix.md).
  --dry-run        Resolve the worktree, diff and prompts, print where they
                   landed, and stop before dispatching an agent.

Local replacement for .github/workflows/pr-review.yml (gate + code-review +
prose-review jobs).  Protocol: local/protocols/review.md.

GitHub is the record (gh_common.py:4-8).  The gate reads the local-ci/summary
commit status on the exact head SHA; the verdict is published as ONE COMMENT
review bound to that SHA plus a local-review/summary status.  Single-account
repos cannot self-APPROVE, so adverseness travels in the status, never in a
review state.  There is no local PR record: a GitHub failure fails this
script closed rather than leaving a fallback record behind.

Exit codes:
  0  review published, or an intentional skip (kill switch, bot commit, stale
     head, empty diff)
  1  usage or environment error
  3  gate blocked: local-ci/summary is not success for the head SHA.  Nothing
     is published — the absence of a green local-review/summary is the block.
  4  the reviewer returned no machine-parseable verdict trailer.  A failing
     local-review/summary is posted so the PR never reads as green.

Environment:
  LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED       disables the reviewer on the literal string
                             "false" only; unset means enabled.
  MIPSTARRE_TRUSTED_REF      git ref the reviewer personas are read from
                             (default: main).  Never the branch under review.
  MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_MODEL     codex model for the code review
                             (default: gpt-5.6-sol)
  MIPSTARRE_PROSE_MODEL      codex model for the blueprint prose review
                             (default: MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_MODEL)
  MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT        runtime state root (default ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev)
  MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_LOCK_WAIT seconds to queue behind another review of the
                             same PR before giving up (default 1800)

1	# codex model comparison — `gpt-5.6-sol` vs `gpt-6-astra`
     2	
     3	Both models run at the same reasoning effort: the global default `model_reasoning_effort = "ultra"` in the codex configuration on ghz applies to every dispatched session, and the owner decided (2026-09-05) not to lower it for the easy sol tasks, so the tables compare sol and astra at ultra effort throughout.
     4	
     5	A side product of the model switch on 2026-09-05: `gpt-6-astra` became the
     6	default for codex sessions at 2026-09-05T15:46Z, and `gpt-5.6-sol` — used for
     7	everything before that — is now kept by operator choice for "really easy"
     8	subagents. This directory answers one question for the owner: **which roles can
     9	sol keep?** It is a rough, re-runnable descriptive comparison, not an
    10	experiment.
    11	
    12	## Re-run
    13	
    14	    python3 results/telemetry/model-comparison/compare.py
    15	
    16	Standard library only, no arguments, finishes in seconds. It prints the report
    17	and rewrites `latest.md`, then appends one dated line to the run log at the
    18	bottom of this file. It reads `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl`, the capture
    19	and rollout event streams, the lane logs under
    20	`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/watchdog/lanes/`, and pull-request state; it writes
    21	nothing outside this directory except a pull-request cache under
    22	`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/model-comparison/`.
    23	
    24	## How the model is derived
    25	
    26	New dispatcher rows in `sessions.jsonl` record the selected model and account.
    27	`compare.py` prefers that explicit identity, retaining fallback for older rows,
    28	and reports how many rows came from each source:
    29	
    30	1. **registry** — the nonempty `model` field, explicitly pinned by the dispatcher.
    31	2. **capture / rollout** — the codex event stream. The rollout named in the
    32	   `rollout` field carries the model in three places (`session_meta`'s
    33	   `base_instructions.provenance.model`, `turn_context.model`,
    34	   `world_state.state.model`). The per-session capture
    35	   (`results/telemetry/sessions/<name>.jsonl`, `codex exec --json`) carries no
    36	   model field today; it is scanned first anyway so a future capture format is
    37	   picked up for free.
    38	3. **lane log** — `dispatch <role> for #N (model <name>, attempt k)` in
    39	   `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/watchdog/lanes/<issue>.lane.log`, used only when every
    40	   such line for that issue names the same model. Lane logs are a runtime cache
    41	   and cover only recent lanes.
    42	4. **time rule** — last resort: sessions starting before 2026-09-05T15:46Z are
    43	   attributed to sol, later ones to astra. This is the weakest source; it cannot
    44	   see a per-dispatch `MIPSTARRE_CODEX_MODEL` override.
    45	
    46	Models other than sol and astra appear as their own rows when they show up
    47	(smoke tests have used `gpt-5.6-luna` and `gpt-5`).
    48	
    49	## Reading the tables
    50	
    51	One table per role. Roles come from `sessions.jsonl`, except that autofix
    52	**fixer** sessions are split out: `local/bin/autofix.sh` dispatches them with
    53	`--role prover --issue pr<N>`, so a prover row whose issue is `pr<N>` is a fixer
    54	and a prover row whose issue is a bare issue number is a lane prover.
    55	
    56	- `in tok med` is `usage.input`, which already includes cached input;
    57	  `cached in` is `sum(cached_input) / sum(input)` over the group.
    58	- Prover and fixer rows get an outcome pair: the share of sessions whose
    59	  worktree branch matches a pull request at all, and the share of those that
    60	  merged. Sessions on branches that were renamed or never pushed show up as not
    61	  opened.
    62	- Reviewer rows get the median number of ledger findings in the review the
    63	  session produced, taken from `results/telemetry/reviews/` when exactly one
    64	  body matches the PR and otherwise from the session's own `.last.md`; `n=` is
    65	  how many sessions it was derivable for. Only three review bodies are archived
    66	  under `results/telemetry/reviews/`, so almost every count comes from
    67	  `.last.md`.
    68	
    69	## The assignment bias — read this before drawing a conclusion
    70	
    71	Models are **not** assigned at random. Sol ran everything up to the switch, so
    72	its rows cover the whole history of the project including its messiest phases;
    73	astra rows start after it. From the switch onward the operator deliberately
    74	sends the *easy* subagents to sol, so any later sol/astra difference measures
    75	the task mix at least as much as the model. Wall time also depends on machine
    76	load, build-cache warmth and lane retries, and token counts depend on how much
    77	context a persona was handed. Treat every number here as descriptive, and use
    78	the outcome and findings columns — not the token or wall-time columns — when
    79	deciding whether sol can keep a role.

#!/bin/sh
set -eu

if [ "${MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS:-}" = "1" ]; then
  # checked-push sets an expected tuple when only the expensive gate is skipped.
  if [ -n "${MIPSTARRE_EXPECTED_PUSH_TUPLE:-}" ]; then
    if ! IFS= read -r ACTUAL_PUSH_TUPLE; then
      echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: checked ref is already current."
      exit 0
    fi
    if IFS= read -r EXTRA_PUSH_TUPLE; then
      echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: expected exactly one advertised ref tuple." >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    if [ "$ACTUAL_PUSH_TUPLE" != "$MIPSTARRE_EXPECTED_PUSH_TUPLE" ]; then
      echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: advertised ref tuple changed after preflight." >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: confirmed preflight ref tuple."
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-push hook skipped by MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS=1."
  exit 0
fi

ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
cd "$ROOT"

CHANGED_FILE_LIST="$(mktemp)"
CHANGED_LEAN_FILE_LIST="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$CHANGED_FILE_LIST" "$CHANGED_LEAN_FILE_LIST"' EXIT
BLUEPRINT_WEB_SMOKE_RAN=0

ZERO_SHA="0000000000000000000000000000000000000000"

run_outside_git_env() (
  for name in $(git rev-parse --local-env-vars); do
    unset "$name"
  done
  "$@"
)

lean_file_to_module() {
  path="${1%.lean}"
  printf '%s\n' "$path" | tr '/' '.'
}

while read LOCAL_REF LOCAL_SHA REMOTE_REF REMOTE_SHA
do
  if [ -z "${LOCAL_SHA:-}" ] || [ "$LOCAL_SHA" = "$ZERO_SHA" ]; then
    continue
  fi

  if [ "$REMOTE_SHA" = "$ZERO_SHA" ]; then
    if git rev-parse --verify origin/main >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      BASE_SHA="$(git merge-base "$LOCAL_SHA" origin/main)"
    else
      BASE_SHA="$(git rev-list --max-parents=0 "$LOCAL_SHA" | tail -n 1)"
    fi
  else
    BASE_SHA="$REMOTE_SHA"
  fi

  git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR "$BASE_SHA" "$LOCAL_SHA" -- >> "$CHANGED_FILE_LIST"
done

sort -u "$CHANGED_FILE_LIST" -o "$CHANGED_FILE_LIST"
grep -E '^(MIPStarRE/.*\.lean|MIPStarRE\.lean)$' "$CHANGED_FILE_LIST" \
  > "$CHANGED_LEAN_FILE_LIST" || true

if [ ! -s "$CHANGED_FILE_LIST" ]; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-push: no changed tracked files detected."
  exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Run the repository's pre-push gate before opening the push transport. Git's
# native pre-push hook runs after receive-pack starts, so a long Lean check can
# leave that connection idle until the remote closes it. This helper preserves
# the gate while keeping the expensive work outside the transport lifetime.
set -euo pipefail

PROG="checked-push.sh"
ZERO_SHA="0000000000000000000000000000000000000000"
SCRIPT_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: local/bin/checked-push.sh [--repo-root PATH] REMOTE LOCAL_REF:REMOTE_REF

Run .githooks/pre-push against one explicit branch ref, then push that ref.
Both refs must use their full refs/heads/... names.
EOF
}

die() {
  printf '%s: error: %s\n' "$PROG" "$*" >&2
  exit 2
}

require_validation_checkout() {
  local checkout_sha checkout_state
  checkout_sha="$(git -C "$VALIDATION_ROOT" rev-parse --verify 'HEAD^{commit}')" ||
    die "cannot resolve HEAD in $VALIDATION_ROOT"
  [ "$checkout_sha" = "$LOCAL_SHA" ] ||
    die "$VALIDATION_ROOT is at $checkout_sha, not $LOCAL_REF at $LOCAL_SHA"
  checkout_state="$(
    git -C "$VALIDATION_ROOT" status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all
  )" || die "cannot inspect working tree $VALIDATION_ROOT"
  [ -z "$checkout_state" ] ||
    die "working tree $VALIDATION_ROOT differs from $LOCAL_REF at $LOCAL_SHA"
}

REPO_ROOT="$SCRIPT_ROOT"
if [ "${1:-}" = "--repo-root" ]; then
  [ "$#" -ge 2 ] || die "--repo-root requires a path"
  REPO_ROOT="$2"
  shift 2
fi

case "${1:-}" in
  --help|-h)
    usage
    exit 0
    ;;
esac
[ "$#" -eq 2 ] || { usage >&2; exit 2; }

REMOTE="$1"
REFSPEC="$2"
case "$REMOTE" in
  ""|-*) die "REMOTE must name a configured Git remote" ;;
esac

LOCAL_REF="${REFSPEC%%:*}"
REMOTE_REF="${REFSPEC#*:}"
if [ "$LOCAL_REF" = "$REFSPEC" ]; then
  die "refspec must map an explicit local branch to an explicit remote branch"
fi
case "$LOCAL_REF:$REMOTE_REF" in
  refs/heads/*:refs/heads/*) ;;
  *) die "both sides of the refspec must start with refs/heads/" ;;
esac

REPO_ROOT="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" rev-parse --show-toplevel)" ||
  die "cannot resolve repository root from $REPO_ROOT"
git -C "$REPO_ROOT" check-ref-format "$LOCAL_REF" >/dev/null ||
  die "invalid local ref $LOCAL_REF"
git -C "$REPO_ROOT" check-ref-format "$REMOTE_REF" >/dev/null ||
  die "invalid remote ref $REMOTE_REF"

if [ "${MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS:-}" = "1" ]; then
  unset MIPSTARRE_EXPECTED_PUSH_TUPLE
  # The bypass skips validation, not the explicit one-ref publication boundary.
  exec git -C "$REPO_ROOT" -c push.followTags=false push --no-follow-tags \
    "$REMOTE" "$REFSPEC"
fi

LOCAL_SHA="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" rev-parse --verify "$LOCAL_REF^{commit}")" ||
  die "cannot resolve local branch $LOCAL_REF"
WORKTREE_ROWS="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" worktree list --porcelain)" ||
  die "cannot list registered worktrees"
VALIDATION_ROOT=""
candidate=""
while IFS= read -r line; do
  case "$line" in
    "worktree "*) candidate="${line#worktree }" ;;
    "branch $LOCAL_REF") VALIDATION_ROOT="$candidate"; break ;;
  esac
done <<< "$WORKTREE_ROWS"
[ -n "$VALIDATION_ROOT" ] ||
  die "$LOCAL_REF is not checked out in a registered worktree"
VALIDATION_ROOT="$(git -C "$VALIDATION_ROOT" rev-parse --show-toplevel)" ||
  die "cannot resolve worktree for $LOCAL_REF"
require_validation_checkout

REMOTE_URL="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" remote get-url --push "$REMOTE")" ||
  die "cannot resolve push URL for remote $REMOTE"
REMOTE_ROWS="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" ls-remote --refs "$REMOTE_URL" "$REMOTE_REF")" ||
  die "cannot read $REMOTE_REF from remote $REMOTE"

REMOTE_SHA=""
while IFS=$'\t' read -r sha ref extra; do
  [ -n "$sha" ] || continue
  [ "$ref" = "$REMOTE_REF" ] || continue
  [ -z "$extra" ] || die "unexpected ls-remote output for $REMOTE_REF"
  [ -z "$REMOTE_SHA" ] || die "remote $REMOTE returned $REMOTE_REF more than once"
  REMOTE_SHA="$sha"
done <<< "$REMOTE_ROWS"
[ -n "$REMOTE_SHA" ] || REMOTE_SHA="$ZERO_SHA"
[[ "$LOCAL_SHA" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || die "unexpected local object id $LOCAL_SHA"
[[ "$REMOTE_SHA" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || die "unexpected remote object id $REMOTE_SHA"
if [ "$REMOTE_SHA" != "$ZERO_SHA" ] &&
    ! git -C "$REPO_ROOT" merge-base --is-ancestor "$REMOTE_SHA" "$LOCAL_SHA"; then
  die "$LOCAL_SHA would not fast-forward $REMOTE_REF from $REMOTE_SHA"
fi

HOOK="$VALIDATION_ROOT/.githooks/pre-push"
[ -x "$HOOK" ] || die "$HOOK is missing or not executable; run scripts/install_git_hooks.sh"

(
  unset MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS
  unset MIPSTARRE_EXPECTED_PUSH_TUPLE
  cd "$VALIDATION_ROOT"
  "$HOOK" "$REMOTE" "$REMOTE_URL"
) <<< "$LOCAL_REF $LOCAL_SHA $REMOTE_REF $REMOTE_SHA"

CURRENT_LOCAL_SHA="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" rev-parse --verify "$LOCAL_REF^{commit}")" ||
  die "cannot re-resolve local branch $LOCAL_REF after preflight"
[ "$CURRENT_LOCAL_SHA" = "$LOCAL_SHA" ] ||
  die "local branch $LOCAL_REF changed during preflight"
require_validation_checkout

printf '%s: gate passed before opening the push transport.\n' "$PROG" >&2
# Freeze the source object and atomically require the preflight remote tip.  The
# native hook is only a short defense-in-depth confirmation; the lease keeps the
# tuple binding intact when that hook is stale or not selected.  Disable implicit
# annotated-tag expansion so the transport contains only the validated ref.
LEASE_SHA="$REMOTE_SHA"
[ "$LEASE_SHA" != "$ZERO_SHA" ] || LEASE_SHA=""
MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS=1 \
  MIPSTARRE_EXPECTED_PUSH_TUPLE="$LOCAL_SHA $LOCAL_SHA $REMOTE_REF $REMOTE_SHA" \
  git -C "$REPO_ROOT" -c push.followTags=false push --no-follow-tags \
    --force-with-lease="$REMOTE_REF:$LEASE_SHA" "$REMOTE" "$LOCAL_SHA:$REMOTE_REF"
